sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: An aromatic perennial with a woody base, usually about 30–120 cm tall. Its deeply divided leaves are silvery and silky; small yellow flower heads grow in branched panicles. Native from Europe and North Africa east to Siberia and the western Himalaya.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: The herb has culinary uses but contains thujone, which can be neurotoxic at high doses. Traditional use or flavouring does not make concentrated preparations safe.

sections.title: Related wormwoods
sections.text: Artemisia vulgaris has green upper leaf surfaces and pale undersides, while A. absinthium is more uniformly silvery. A. maritima is another low-growing, silvery species associated with salt-marsh habitats.
